$comment: Nets held out of autorouting, per R9. This file is the single source of
truth for the strip (tools/kicad_strip.py) and the router (tools/kicad_route.py)
so both agree on exactly one net set -- a mismatch between them would void
'preserve' means the existing copper was audited and is good.
'preserve_flagged' means it is held out of the router because an autorouter
would make it worse, NOT because it is correct. Excluding a net is not the
same as blessing it -- these carry real defects that survive the strip into
both sides of the comparison, which keeps the comparison fair while leaving
the board wrong. Each one names its defect so it can be fixed deliberately.

exclusions.reason: USB 2.0 high-speed pair, 480 Mbps. 118.74 / 118.48 mm, 0.22% skew, both entirely on the top layer with zero vias. Textbook; an autorouter can only degrade it. Note EasyEDA's own DRC still flags a length discrepancy on this pair against its configured rule, so 'good' here means good relative to the rest of the board, not signed off.

exclusions.defect: Asymmetric layer transition: USB_DP_CONN takes 2 vias down to the bottom layer over 1.7 mm while USB_DM_CONN stays entirely on top with none. At 480 Mbps this causes impedance discontinuity and common-mode conversion, and matters more than the 0.39 mm length skew does.

exclusions.reason: Parallel bus to NOR flash; wants group length matching and a consistent reference plane.
exclusions.defect: 29 mm length spread across the bus (IO3 10.14 mm to NCS 39.48 mm) and five different layer strategies -- CLK on Inner1, NCS on Inner2, IO1/IO3 on the bottom layer, IO2 entirely on top. Different reference planes means different impedance per bit line.

exclusions.reason: Debug interface. Low speed and non-critical, but hand-routed and not worth re-solving. SWO is a single-pin net with no copper; listed so the router never invents a route for it.
Oscillator loop. Loop area drives EMI and startup margin, so this is never an autorouter's job.
exclusions.defect: OSC_OUT is 11.17 mm against OSC_IN's 6.39 mm, with 2 vias and 5.3 mm on the bottom layer. A crystal loop wants to be short, single-layer, and tight against its load caps; this one leaves the layer and comes back.

exclusions.reason: Differential pairs. Electrically the mildest group here -- at CAN's ~1 Mbps, 2 mm of skew is roughly 13 ps and irrelevant -- but an autorouter would not route them as pairs at all.
exclusions.defect: Both _H legs carry vias and layer changes their _L partners do not, and CAN1 has 8.62% length skew (25.24 vs 23.06 mm). Evidence the pairs were not routed as pairs. Separately, kicad-happy reports neither transceiver (U8, U9) has 120R termination.

$notes.power_nets_are_not_excluded: GND, +3V3, +5V and the other rails are stripped along with everything else. Their copper pours are zones, not tracks, and the strip does not touch zones -- only routed segments and vias.
$notes.single_pin_nets: TT1-8, BTN1-4 and SWO have one pad and no copper. Nothing to strip and nothing to route; they are incomplete connections in the schematic, not routing work.
$notes.keepouts: Two rule areas exist on Inner2. Six vias currently sit inside one of them (an existing violation, not caused by the strip). Any router run must not add more.
